Thanks for the questionnaire. Looping in Karhtik (Solutions Architect) and Marissa (VP Product) to provide the technical fill and compliance artifacts. We'll populate the spreadsheet and return the table plus a one-page narrative by the 14th. High level answers below to set expectations:

- RTO (control plane): 1–4 minutes for management plane failover; full control-plane reconvergence typically within 10–30 minutes depending on upstream DNS TTL and regional health checks.
- RTO (data/model serving): warm-standby regional pools give 30s–3min token-serving continuity for most traffic; cold-start recovery for fully provisioned dedicated capacity can be 20–45 minutes.
- RPO (model state & embeddings): for customer embeddings and persistent state we target sub-5s replication for hot regions (via async streaming to durable stores), and up to 5 minutes for background replication during heavy load.

We'll attach an RTO-RPO table and the Redwood DR overview and SOC2 audit summary with dates of last tests. If HorizonTech wants a tabletop exercise, Jonas (CSM) and I can run one next week — suggest 2026-07-16 or 2026-07-17.

Stephanie —

Drafted the spreadsheet entries and a short technical narrative. Paste below the key items I put into RTO-RPO_Table.xlsx (please sanity check before we send):

--- RTO / RPO table (summary) ---
Control plane (api control & config): RTO target = 1–5 minutes; RPO = 0 (config changes are stored in strongly-consistent region-local datastore with synchronous write to standby control replicas).
Model serving (hosted inference endpoints): RTO target = 30s–3 minutes (active-passive with warm standby; auto-failover triggered by regional health check and routing policy); RPO = near-zero for model binaries (we keep versioned artifacts in replicated object storage).
Embedding store (customer vectors): RTO = 1–10 minutes depending on profile; RPO = up to 5 seconds for streaming-enabled customers, up to 5 minutes for batched-sync customers.
Data plane session continuity: sessions using long-lived streaming may need client reconnection; KV cache is replicated per-region with time-limited cold-cache penalty (~1–2 tokens extra latency while cache rebuilds).

Failover mechanics (high level):
- Health detection: active agent + global health checks detect region degradation.
- Routing: primary policy is region affinity; on failure we switch to secondary region via global LB with weighted routing + DNS failover (TTL 30s recommended).
- State reconciliation: streaming replication of embeddings to durable store; for in-memory KV caches we rely on prefix caching and rehydration.
- Capacity: warm standby is kept at configurable percent of base capacity (customer-configurable in Dedicated); burst provisioning limits cold-start time.

Testing & evidence:
- Quarterly full failover test for Dedicated customers (last test: 2026-04-09, outcome: <10min control-plane reconverge).
- SOC2 Type II report covering 2025–2026 period attached (SOC2-Audit-Summary.pdf).

Open items we should confirm with Elaine: desired DNS TTL on their side, whether they require active-active global read routing, and whether they want documented runbook steps for automated vs manual failover.

-Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Tom / Elaine —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Attached are the consolidated deliverables: Redwood_DR_Overview_v2.pdf (one-page narrative + diagram), RTO-RPO_Table.xlsx (detailed targets and notes), SOC2-Audit-Summary.pdf, and a short runbook excerpt pasted below. Also included a quick breakdown of the cold-start timing for Dedicated reserved capacity.

Cold-start breakdown (Dedicated reserved capacity):
- Provisioning GPU host(s): ~8–20 minutes (depends on cloud region and current capacity slate).
- Model artifact download & integrity checks: ~3–8 minutes (models are sharded; parallel fetch).
- JIT compilation & kernel selection (optimized paths): ~5–15 minutes for large models without cached compilation; greatly reduced if compilation cache present.
- Routing & warm-up (reassigning traffic + KV cache rehydration): ~2–10 minutes.
Estimated total: 18–45 minutes typical; 75th percentile under heavy region allocation pressure ~60 minutes.

Runbook excerpt (top-level):
1) Detect: automated health probes mark region degraded -> alert page.
2) Assess: determine degradation class (control plane vs data plane vs disk-only).
3) Trigger: automatic or manual failover policy (per-customer policy setting).
4) Route: invoke global LB weight switch and optionally change DNS record; validate upstream checks.
5) Recover: bring warm standby capacity up to 100%, rehydrate caches, reconcile streaming replication offsets.
6) Postmortem: capture timeline, persistence checks, and customer-impact metrics.

Tabletop slots (available):
- 2026-07-16 10:00–11:30 PT
- 2026-07-16 15:00–16:30 PT
- 2026-07-17 09:30–11:00 PT
